reviewer_reports.summary: The new batching logic can emit over-budget batches in a non-edge case, which breaks the stated size contract and can regress provider calls. I also found a verification fallback routing bug where a 2-seat panel can choose the wrong lens fallback for the second seat.

findings.title: Unplaceable oversized piece is appended to a fresh batch without any size guard
findings.evidence: When `_split_section` returns an unplaceable whole section, `_batch_sections_detailed` still does `current += piece` after only checking `if current and len(current) + len(piece) > max_chars`, so an oversized `piece` is accepted into an empty batch and exceeds the budget.
findings.recommendation: Before appending a piece, also handle the empty-batch case: if `len(piece) > max_chars`, mark batching incomplete and either return a dedicated failure path or keep the over-budget piece out of normal batches so downstream provider requests never exceed `max_chars`.

findings.title: Verification fallback lens mapping is wrong for the second seat in a 2-provider panel
findings.evidence: The new mapping assigns each provider only `list(LENSES)[_i % len(LENSES)]`, but the comment says two seats split the lenses. With two providers and more than two lenses, seat 0 gets only the first lens and seat 1 gets only the second, so findings from other lenses raised by those seats will look up the wrong fallback or none at all.
findings.recommendation: Reuse the exact review-round seat-to-lens assignment logic from `_reviewer_tasks` instead of reconstructing it here. In particular, for 2 seats each seat should own the same lens set it would in review, not a single modulo-selected lens.
